title: Anchor v1
description: Where a capture sits in one edition's bytes (plan 7.5, 9.1-9.3, 10.1-10.2; ADR-0004, ADR-0005, ADR-0006, ADR-0016). A discriminated union on `kind`: `epub`, `pdf`, `text` (TXT and Markdown) and `audio`. Every anchor names its schema version, its Work and Edition, and the asset or assets and the SHA-256 of the bytes it was taken from; an anchor is exact only for those bytes. Each kind has a small portable part that any client can read and, where a reader produced one, the reader's own locator verbatim in `reader.locator`, which only the adapter named in `reader.adapter` interprets. Text offsets always state their unit and count Unicode scalars (`unicode_scalar`); native UTF-16 ranges appear only inside `reader.locator`. Optional fields are omitted when unknown, never written as null: a missing location stays missing and is never invented (a PDF without /PageLabels has no `page_label`). Compatibility: a reader accepts an anchor whose `kind` it does not know (any lowercase token), keeps it unchanged, never re-anchors, rewrites or draws it, and still shows the capture that holds it; a v1 writer emits only the four kinds above (`$defs/known_kind`). Readers tolerate unknown optional fields (Contracts/README.md). Each member of the top-level `allOf` has a `title`, which the checker uses to name the rule an invalid fixture breaks. Rules JSON Schema cannot express are checked in code by `Scripts/check-spike-anchors.py` (rule IDs in ADR-0016 section 5): U1 every string is a sequence of Unicode scalar values (no unpaired surrogate escape such as \ud800); A1 every range has start < end; A2 a scalar range covers the text it locates: a PDF `text_range` has as many scalars as its segment's `text`, a text `text_range` as many as `exact_text`, and an EPUB `text_offsets` as many as `exact_text` after whitespace collapsing (see `$defs/epub`); A3 a PDF anchor's `exact_text` is its segments' texts joined with a single U+000A; A4 PDF segments are in document order (page index non-decreasing; on one page, ranges increasing and not overlapping); A5 an EPUB `segment.index` is below `segment.count`; A6 an audio anchor's ranges name distinct assets, every range after the first starts at 0 ms (a cross-file selection is a contiguous span of the timeline at capture time), and their total length is at most 120,000 ms (plan 10.2); A7 a PDF line rectangle lies within its page box: x + w <= 1 and y + h <= 1, with a tolerance of 0.000001 for the 6-decimal rounding of each component.

schema_version.description: Version of this anchor format. A reader refuses a version it does not know. Appendix A.1 and the Stage 0 spikes called this field `version`.

kind.description: Discriminator. Known kinds: `$defs/known_kind`. Any other lowercase token is an anchor kind from a later writer, preserved unchanged and never resolved.

edition_id.description: The edition whose bytes the anchor locates. Required for every known kind: offsets, pages and timelines are edition-specific (plan 7.1, 7.5, 13.3; G0.5 AI finding F23).

uuid.description: Lowercase UUID generated on device (plan 7.3). Swift writers lowercase `uuidString`, which is uppercase.

known_kind.description: The anchor kinds a v1 writer emits.

not_secret_name.description: No field may carry a credential (Contracts/README.md, Secrets). The same names as the context-pack contract's pattern, matched without regard to case, written out letter by letter because the `(?i)` flag that pattern uses is not ECMA-262, JSON Schema's regular-expression dialect, so a JavaScript validator cannot compile it (ADR-0016). Each letter's class holds exactly the characters Python's case-insensitive match accepts for it, so the dotted and dotless I (U+0130, U+0131), the Kelvin sign (U+212A) and the long s (U+017F) count too. The checker derives this form from the context-pack pattern on every CI run and compares.

scalar_range.description: Half-open range [start, end) in Unicode scalars (code-checked: start < end, rule A1).

context_text.description: Text before or after the located text, exactly as the reader or extraction returned it (raw whitespace kept). May be empty at the start or end of a resource, page or file.

exact_text.description: The located text exactly as selected: never trimmed, collapsed, normalized or truncated (plan 9.1, I-05). Compared scalar for scalar, not by canonical equivalence.

reader.description: The reader adapter's own locator, stored verbatim (plan 7.5). Adapter-opaque: other clients do not interpret `locator`; they use the portable fields.

normalized_rect.description: [x, y, w, h] as fractions of the page box, origin at its lower-left, y up, in the page's unrotated space (ADR-0005), 6 decimals. Within the box (code-checked: x + w <= 1 and y + h <= 1 within 0.000001, rule A7): a writer clamps a line box that reaches past the CropBox (the part outside is not displayed).

epub.description: One anchor per EPUB resource (ADR-0004 section 3; G0.1 EPUB `anchor-samples.json`). A quotation that continues into the next resource is several anchors, one per resource, each with `segment`, because each resource has its own reader locator. Re-anchoring order: `reader.locator`, then `exact_text` with `prefix` and `suffix` inside `resource_href`, then `text_offsets` when its `extraction_version` matches (plan 7.5). Readium 3.11.0 copies `href` from the navigator's current location, so the adapter confirms the resource before writing (G0.1 EPUB finding F1) and re-anchoring treats `resource_href` as fallible. `progression`, `total_progression` and `position` are display and coarse-fallback values that change with layout; `position` is Readium's synthetic position and is never shown as a page number (plan 7.5).

asset_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the EPUB file's bytes. A different digest is a different asset: same-asset rules no longer apply.

resource_href.description: The resource the text is in, relative to the publication root, as normalized by the reader.

resource_media_type.description: The resource's media type from the manifest, as the reader serves it (Readium's locator `type`).

exact_text.description: The selected text as the reader returned it (Readium: `window.getSelection().toString()`, the rendered text).

prefix.description: Text before the selection as the reader returned it (Readium: up to about 200 UTF-16 code units of raw DOM text).

suffix.description: Text after the selection, as for `prefix`.

text_offsets.description: Where the selection sits in Sylvia's own extraction of `resource_href`: block `block_index`, half-open range [start, end) in Unicode scalars of that block's text. The rendered selection and the extraction can differ in whitespace, so the adapter (G0.1 `CaptureBuilder.offsets`) looks for `exact_text` with its whitespace collapsed (each maximal run of Unicode White_Space characters replaced by one U+0020, leading and trailing ones removed), choosing among several occurrences by the prefix; the range covers that collapsed text (rule A2). Omitted when the selection spans extraction blocks or is ambiguous there (G0.1 EPUB finding F10); the locator and the text with its context still anchor it.

progression.description: Readium's progression in the resource of the page shown at capture time (not the selection's own position). Omitted when the adapter had to correct the resource.

total_progression.description: Progression in the publication of the page shown at capture time. Display only.

position.description: Readium's synthetic position (about 1,024 characters each). Never shown as a page number.

segment.description: Present when one quotation is stored as several anchors: this anchor's place among them (code-checked: index < count, rule A5; in a capture, rule C3).

reader.description: `adapter` names the reader (G0.1: `readium-swift`), `adapter_version` its release (G0.1: `3.11.0`), `locator` Readium's Locator JSON verbatim. `adapter` and `locator` are required by `$defs/reader`; an EPUB anchor also requires `adapter_version`, because Readium's locator format changes between releases.

pdf.description: One anchor per selection, with one segment per contiguous text range per page in document order (ADR-0005; G0.1 PDF `anchor-samples.json`). Re-anchoring order: same digests and the stored range rebuilt into identical text; otherwise the segment text with its exact prefix and suffix found exactly once in the same asset; several matches or bare-text matches give "Location needs review"; a different asset digest is never relocated automatically (plan 7.5).

asset_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the PDF file's bytes.

exact_text.description: The quotation exactly as selected: the segments' texts joined with a single U+000A (ADR-0005; code-checked, rule A3).

extraction.description: Which text extraction `text_range` indexes. PDFKit's extractor ships with the OS, so the platform build is part of it.

platform.description: OS name, version and build, for example `iOS 26.5 (23F77)`.

page_label.description: The printed label from the file's /PageLabels. Omitted when the file supplies none: Sylvia never stores a label PDFKit invents ("1", "2", ...).

page_box.description: The box the rectangles are normalized to, in PDF user-space points.

rect.description: [x, y, width, height] of the CropBox.

text.description: This segment's text, equal to the page text at `text_range`.

text_range.description: Half-open range into the page's extracted text (`extraction`).

prefix.description: Page text before the segment (the G0.1 builder stores up to 32 scalars; the length is the writer's choice).

suffix.description: Page text after the segment, as for `prefix`.

line_rects.description: One rectangle per selected line. A client draws a stored rect on a page shown rotated by R clockwise, normalized to the displayed page with origin top-left, as: R=0 (x, 1-y-h, w, h); R=90 (y, x, h, w); R=180 (1-x-w, y, w, h); R=270 (1-y-h, 1-x-w, h, w) (ADR-0005).

page_text_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the page text's UTF-8 bytes; a mismatch means the extraction changed and `text_range` is not trusted.

reader.description: `adapter` names the reader (G0.1: `pdfkit`), `locator` holds PDFKit's native ranges (G0.1: `{"utf16_ranges": [{"page_index", "location", "length"}]}`).

text.description: A selection in a TXT or Markdown file (plan 9.3, 7.5). Offsets index the decoded source text that Sylvia retains (for Markdown the source, not the rendered output), so a renderer change never moves a quote. `exact_text` is that source text at `text_range`, so any client can check it against the retained bytes without a renderer (rule A2). For Markdown it therefore keeps the markup inside the selection: a selection made in the rendered view is stored as the source span the reader maps it to, for example `for *absolute freedom* and wildness` with its asterisks, never as the rendered words alone, whose length would not match the range; how the reader maps a rendered selection to a source span is the adapter's (its locator stays in `reader`). Designed from plan 9.3 and the EPUB and PDF anchors: no Stage 0 spike produced a text anchor (ADR-0016).

asset_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's original bytes.

exact_text.description: The decoded source text at `text_range`, exactly; for Markdown with its markup (rule A2).

text_range.description: Half-open range into the decoded source text.

source_text.description: The decoded text `text_range` indexes: `extraction_version` names the decoder and its settings, `text_sha256` is the SHA-256 of that text's UTF-8 bytes, so a changed decoding is detected before the range is trusted.

audio.description: An audio selection in asset-local integer milliseconds (plan 7.5, 10.1-10.2; ADR-0006 decision 11). A selection that crosses files is several ordered ranges, each bound to its member asset and that asset's digest; nothing here depends on the order of an edition's members, so a reorder never rewrites a stored anchor. The digest is the imported asset of record's: a derived playback copy (ADR-0006 decision 17, an import remux) has the same timing and does not change it. `timeline_revision` is the edition timeline revision the user saw at capture time, for display only.

items.description: Half-open range [start_ms, end_ms) in one asset (code-checked: start_ms < end_ms, rule A1).
